79068-katy-hunter-s-homes.title: Katy Hunter'S Homes.
79068-katy-hunter-s-homes.creator: Unknown
79068-katy-hunter-s-homes.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. They were a very happy little family. But in a wild storm the vessel was lost, and Katy's papa went down with it. Hunter had to set herself to work in earnest, to earn a living for herself and baby. She struggled along for a time, not finding much to do, although she understood the dress-maker's trade.

arxiv-2105-11435.title: Electron affinity of oganesson
arxiv-2105-11435.creator: M. Y. Kaygorodov, L. V. Skripnikov, I. I. Tupitsyn, E. Eliav, Y. S. Kozhedub, A. V. Malyshev, A. V. Oleynichenko, V. M. Shabaev, A. V. Titov, A. V. Zaitsevskii
arxiv-2105-11435.description: Abstract The electron affinity (EA) of superheavy element Og is calculated by the use of the relativistic Fock-space coupled cluster (FSCC) and configuration interaction methods. The FSCC cluster operator expansion included single, double, and triple excitations treated in a non-perturbative manner. The Gaunt and retardation electron-electron interactions are taken into account.

arxiv-2202-05218.title: Pynguin: Automated Unit Test Generation for Python Conference: 44th International Conference on Software Engineering Companion; May 21–29, 2022; Pittsburgh, PA, USA 44th International Conference on Software Engineering Companion (ICSE ’22 Companion), May 21–29, 2022, Pittsburgh, PA, USA Price: 15.00
arxiv-2202-05218.creator: Stephan Lukasczyk, Gordon Fraser
arxiv-2202-05218.description: Abstract . Automated unit test generation is a well-known methodology aiming to reduce the developers’ effort of writing tests manually. Prior research focused mainly on statically typed programming languages like Java. In practice, however, dynamically typed languages have received a huge gain in popularity over the last decade.

arxiv-2205-05688.title: Quantum complexity and topological phases of matter
arxiv-2205-05688.creator: Pawel Caputa and Sinong Liu
arxiv-2205-05688.description: Abstract In this work, we find that the complexity of quantum many-body states, defined as a spread in the Krylov basis, may serve as a new probe that distinguishes topological phases of matter. We illustrate this analytically in one of the representative examples, the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, finding that spread complexity becomes constant in the topological phase.

arxiv-2212-08621.description: Abstract The ALICE ITS3 (Inner Tracking System 3) upgrade project and the CERN EP R&D on monolithic pixel sensors are investigating the feasibility of the Tower Partners Semiconductor Co. 65 nm 65\text{\,}\mathrm{nm} process for use in the next generation of vertex detectors.

arxiv-2301-09292.title: Investigating time variability of X-ray absorption in Swift GRBs Facilities: Swift(XRT) XSPEC ( Arnaud 1996 ) , pymultinest ( Buchner et al. 2014 )
arxiv-2301-09292.creator: Vlasta Valan, Josefin Larsson, Björn Ahlgren
arxiv-2301-09292.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Vlasta Valan, Josefin Larsson, Björn Ahlgren. The existence of excess absorption in the X-ray spectra of GRBs is well known, but the primary location of the absorbing material is still uncertain. To gain more knowledge about this, we have performed a time-resolved analysis of the X-ray spectra of 199 GRBs observed by the Swift X-ray telescope, searching for evidence of a decreasing column density ( N H , intr N_{\mathrm{H,intr}} ) that would indicate that the GRBs are ionizing matter in their surroundings.

arxiv-2312-16047.title: 2D-guided 3D Gaussian Segmentation
arxiv-2312-16047.description: Abstract Recently, 3D Gaussian, as an explicit 3D representation method, has demonstrated strong competitiveness over NeRF (Neural Radiance Fields) in terms of expressing complex scenes and training duration. These advantages signal a wide range of applications for 3D Gaussians in 3D understanding and editing. Meanwhile, the segmentation of 3D Gaussians is still in its infancy.

arxiv-2403-15047.title: Atom Number Fluctuations in Bose Gases - Statistical analysis of parameter estimation
arxiv-2403-15047.creator: T. Vibel, M. B. Christensen, R. M. F. Andersen, L. N. Stokholm, K. Pawłowski, K. Rzążewski, M. A. Kristensen, J. J. Arlt
arxiv-2403-15047.description: Abstract The investigation of the fluctuations in interacting quantum systems at finite temperatures showcases the ongoing challenges in understanding complex quantum systems. Recently, atom number fluctuations in weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates were observed, motivating an investigation of the thermal component of partially condensed Bose gases.

arxiv-2410-02058.title: On the Hausdorff dimension and attracting laminations for fully irreducible automorphisms of free groups
arxiv-2410-02058.creator: Ilya Kapovich
arxiv-2410-02058.description: Abstract Motivated by a classic theorem of Birman and Series about the set of complete simple geodesics on a hyperbolic surface, we study the Hausdorff dimension of the set of endpoints in ∂ F r \partial F_{r} of some abstract algebraic laminations associated with free group automorphisms.

arxiv-2503-16883.title: Assessing the Reliability and Validity of GPT-4 in Annotating Emotion Appraisal Ratings
arxiv-2503-16883.creator: Deniss Ruder, Andero Uusberg, Kairit Sirts
arxiv-2503-16883.description: Abstract Appraisal theories suggest that emotions arise from subjective evaluations of events, referred to as appraisals. The taxonomy of appraisals is quite diverse, and they are usually given ratings on a Likert scale to be annotated in an experiencer-annotator or reader-annotator paradigm.

This size restriction limits their molecular genetic and biotechnological utility, such as numerous...

pmc-10531908.title: Short Survey on the Protein Modifications in Plasma during SARS-CoV-2 Infection
pmc-10531908.creator: Agnieszka Gęgotek, Neven Zarkovic, Biserka Orehovec, Morana Jaganjac, Suzana Borovic Sunjic, Elżbieta Skrzydlewska, Manuela Rizzi, Pier Paolo Sainaghi
pmc-10531908.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, it is important to understand the pathology of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection associated with respiratory failure and high mortality. The plasma proteome, including protein modification by lipid peroxidation products in COVID-19 survivors (COVID-19; n = 10) and deceased individuals (CovDeath; n = 10) was compared in samples collected upon admission to the hospital, when there was no difference in their status, with that of healthy individuals (Ctr; n = 10).

pmc-10740616.title: Evolutionary Plasticity in Insular Lizard, Adapting over Reproduction, Metabolism, and Color Variation
pmc-10740616.creator: Domenico Fulgione, Valeria Maselli, Eleonora Rivieccio, Serena Aceto, Marco Salvemini, Maria Buglione, Vincent L Bels
pmc-10740616.description: Simple SummaryThe recent debate on the theory of evolution focuses on various aspects that arise following the evidence of the advancement of knowledge in genetics and molecular biology. In particular, some researchers are inclined to introduce an extended evolutionary theory involving this hypothesis. Many theoretical hypotheses are based on the ever-increasing knowledge of phenotypic plasticity as well as epigenetic mechanisms.

pmc-11326815.title: Host Transcriptional Meta-signatures Reveal Diagnostic Biomarkers for Plasmodium falciparum Malaria
pmc-11326815.creator: Nágila Isleide Silva, Pedro Felipe Loyola Souza, Bárbara Fernandes Silva, Simone Gonçalves Fonseca, Luiz Gustavo Gardinassi
pmc-11326815.description: BackgroundTranscriptomics has been used to evaluate immune responses during malaria in diverse cohorts worldwide. However, the high heterogeneity of cohorts and poor generalization of transcriptional signatures reported in each study limit their potential clinical applications.MethodsWe compiled 28 public data sets containing 1556 whole-blood or peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptome samples.

pmc-11548141.title: Prediction of the Remaining Useful Life of Bearings Through CNN-Bi-LSTM-Based Domain Adaptation Model
pmc-11548141.creator: Feifan Li, Zhuoheng Dai, Lei Jiang, Chanfei Song, Caiming Zhong, Yingna Chen, Heinrich Wörtche
pmc-11548141.description: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of mechanical bearings is crucial in the industry. Estimating the RUL enables the assessment of health bearing, maintenance planning, and significant cost reduction, thereby fostering industrial development. Existing models rely on traditional feature engineering with feature changes because operating conditions pose a major challenge to the generalization of RUL prediction models.

pmc-11654710.title: Pertactin deficiency of Bordetella pertussis: Insights into epidemiology, and perspectives on surveillance and public health impact
pmc-11654710.creator: Ulrich Heininger, Helena Martini, Jennifer Eeuwijk, Ivana Prokić, Adrienne P Guignard, Elisa Turriani, Maurine Duchenne, Valérie Berlaimont
pmc-11654710.description: Pertussis resurgence has been documented even in countries with high pediatric vaccine coverage. The proportion of Bordetella pertussis isolates not expressing pertactin (PRN) has increased in several countries where acellular pertussis (aP) vaccines are used. We systematically reviewed published literature up to July 2023 on PRN-negative B.

pmc-12659321.title: Six-month readmission and associated factors among psychiatry patients at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, Western Kenya
pmc-12659321.creator: Angeline Tenge, Joice Baliddawa, Rodgers Songole, Lukoye Atwoli, Michael Odawa
pmc-12659321.description: BackgroundHospital readmissions due to mental illnesses increase the burden and costs of patient management globally. While the transition to community-based mental health care is a key focus, readmission rates remain high. Understanding the risk factors associated with readmission to mental health units can help healthcare workers implement effective measures to reduce readmissions, enhance patient outcomes, and strengthen community-based care.

pmc-12710329.title: Spatiotemporal development of late and moderate preterm infant gut and oral microbiomes and impact of gestational age on early colonization
pmc-12710329.creator: Sinéad Ahearn-Ford, Andreas Kakaroukas, Gregory R. Young, Andrew Nelson, Marieke Abrahamse-Berkeveld, Ruurd M. van Elburg, Darren Smith, Janet E. Berrington, Nicholas D. Embleton, Christopher J. Stewart
pmc-12710329.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Microbiome research focusing on late and moderate preterm infants (LMPT; 32 to 36 weeks gestation) is limited, despite rising LMPT births, large healthcare burdens, and increased risks of multiple morbidities, potentially microbially related. In this longitudinal cohort study, 16S rRNA gene sequencing was used to analyze 371 stool and 402 saliva samples from 160 LMPT infants, collected at five time points between birth and 12 months corrected age (CA), to describe spatial and temporal variability in gut and oral microbiomes.

pmc-13223130.title: Arthroscopic one-stage management of diffuse shoulder pigmented villonodular synovitis with concomitant full-thickness rotator cuff tear and acromial bone erosion: a rare case report
pmc-13223130.creator: Chenglong Wang, Xiaoping Zhou, Jialin Zhuang, Yang Ding, Fulin Tang
pmc-13223130.description: The coexistence of diffuse shoulder pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS), full-thickness rotator cuff tear, and PVNS-induced focal acromial bone erosion is extremely rare, with no prior reports documenting this complete pathological triad, which poses unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a 52-year-old male with a three-month history of progressive right shoulder pain, swelling, and functional limitation.

pmc-13292729.title: ICF-based functioning profiles in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: Evidence from a population-based study in Argentina
pmc-13292729.creator: Leidy Johana Escobar Zuluaga, María de las Mercedes Ruiz Brunner, Eduardo Cuestas, Elisabeth Cieri, Ana Laura Condinanzi, Carolina Ayllon, Verónica Schiariti
pmc-13292729.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Purpose:In Argentina, there is no consensus on the functional assessment of children with cerebral palsy (CP). The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) Core Sets for children with CP are tools that standardize clinical functional assessments. The aim was to build functioning profiles of children with CP aged 2 to 18 years in eight Argentine cities, to identify their functional needs and contribute to improving assessment processes.Methods:Cross-sectional study, developed in stages.

pmc-13475508.title: Timing of cognitive decline onset and life-course trajectories A pooled longitudinal analysis of 14,389 adults across three cohorts
pmc-13475508.creator: Jan Sebastian Novotný, Sivan Klil-Drori, Yonas Endale Geda, Ziad Nasreddine, Gorazd Bernard Stokin
pmc-13475508.description: Highlights•Measurable decline in global cognition emerges as early as the fourth decade of life (aged 31-40).•Cognitive decline shows domain-specific asynchrony: non-memory domains exhibit significant attrition nearly two decades before detectable changes in episodic memory.•Early monitoring of multidomain cognitive health – rather than a late-life focus on memory alone – may be essential for proactive dementia prevention.
